title: Projectile Target Challenge: Pick Angle and Speed
description: A launcher sits at the left end of a flat 70 m green field with white distance marks every 10 m. A blue target disc with a yellow flag sits down the field. Set the launch angle (the barrel tilts) and speed, then press Launch: a red ball flies along its arc, leaving a red trail; the previous shot's arc stays as a faded ghost line. Readouts give landing distance, miss distance and side, flight time, peak height, launches used and targets hit.

game.objective: Hit 3 targets (30 m, 45 m, then 18 m) using no more than 10 launches. A hit lands within 1.5 m of the target centre.
game.hint: At the same speed, angles adding to 90° (like 30° and 60°) land at the same distance, and 45° goes farthest. Doubling the speed makes the shot go four times as far.

assumptions: Simplified simulation: no air resistance, and the ball starts at ground level on flat ground.
Gravity is 9.8 m/s² straight down; the horizontal speed stays constant and only the vertical speed changes.
Each point of the flight comes exactly from the projectile formulas, so the landing distance equals speed² × sin(2 × angle) ÷ 9.8.
The ball is treated as a point (drawn enlarged so it is easy to see); the flight ends the moment it returns to ground height. A hit is a landing within 1.5 m of the target centre, both edges counted.
Every flight is shown over 2 seconds of screen time, so screen time does not match the flight-time readout. Real balls are slowed by air and land shorter than shown.
Targets come in a fixed order (30 m, 45 m, 18 m); Reset starts the same challenge again and clears the score and both arcs.
